To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the probability representation of non-relativistic quantum mechanics is equivalent to classical statistical mechanics and that the classical propagator is the Green function for the evolution of the MDF.

(i) the classical propagator is the Green function of an evolution equation for the MDF; (ii) the MDF for an initial pure state is the Wigner function for the density matrix; (iii) the classical propagators for the forced harmonic oscillator are found and the MDF for the coherent and Fock initial states are obtained.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of time-dependent invariants in the probability representation and the explicit construction of the corresponding Green functions.
the development of a new representation of quantum mechanics based on a classical probability distribution function.
the development of a classical description of quantum mechanics, which is based on the probability distribution function and is free from the usual difficulties of the classical limit.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the probability representation of nonrelativistic quantum mechanics is an effective classical theory, in the sense that all its predictions are contained in the classical propagator.

the probability representation of the quantum mechanics provides a very useful and effective tool for the description of quantum phenomena, and that the MDF is the natural object to describe quantum coherence and entanglement.

the probability representation provides a new perspective on quantum mechanics, which is useful for the understanding of the quantum-classical transition and for the development of a consistent quantum theory of measurement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the probability representation of QM is a classical probability theory, whose classical dynamics is governed by an equation of the Liouville type.
we provide a classical description for quantum states, and we find the time-dependent invariants of such a description.

the probability representation of non-relativistic quantum mechanics is a classical theory, in which the quantum states are represented as classical probability distributions, whose dynamics is governed by a Fokker-Planck equation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the probability representation is a useful tool to investigate quantum mechanics, and it may help us understand the quantum-classical transition.

, in spite of the fact that in the probability representation quantum states are represented as classical probability distributions, the quantum evolution is still governed by a quantum equation, the Schr\"{o}dinger equation.
, in a large class of systems, the quantum evolution of the density matrix can be obtained by a classical evolution of a classical probability distribution.
